claims.text: The platform's own recorded distances establish a deviation of 1.90 km on this trip — actual_distance_km 24.3 km against optimal_distance_km 22.4 km — which is almost double the 1.0 km tolerance in POL-RD-22. The trip is therefore outside tolerance, and the 'within tolerance' rows of POL-RD-24 are not available to the driver.

The driver-device trace independently shows which route was actually taken: after the PIE the vehicle ran Loyang Avenue and Loyang Way instead of the recommended Tampines Expressway, rejoining the recommended route only at Pasir Ris Close. That matches the platform's route_deviation_detected event at 01:38:36 and route_rejoined event at 01:44:03, so the route deviation is not in dispute on the record.

The reroute was not traffic-justified. The only traffic data for the trip window is EV-ADVIS-05013-01, an LTA advisory of type NONE whose own message records 'no incident, roadwork or closure' and speed bands 6-8 for the queried segment. POL-RD-23 requires congestion, an incident or a closure on the recommended route segment at the trip time, and a type of NONE is not one of the kinds POL-RD-23 names.

The driver did not inform the rider before or at the point of deviation, as POL-RD-21 requires. The deviation was detected at 01:38:36, but the driver's first and only chat message is at 01:42:36 — four minutes after the deviation began and only after two messages from the rider. No in-app call was placed at all (in_app_calls is empty), so the contact obligation is unmet on the chat log itself.

The rider raised the deviation and the driving contemporaneously and the driver dismissed both: 'Uncle where are you going? This is not the way' at 01:40:46 (read 01:41:18) and 'Please slow down, you are driving very fast and I feel scared' at 01:41:36 (read 01:42:05), answered at 01:42:36 with 'Relax lah short cut only'. The driver's reply confirms the detour was a shortcut, not a traffic response, and POL-RD-23 provides that a driver's assertion of traffic with no supporting traffic data does not justify a reroute. No rider acknowledgment of the deviation appears anywhere in the log.

On the POL-RD-24 matrix this case falls in row (d) — not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km — so the excess distance fare is refundable in full to the rider: 1.90 km x 0.72 SGD per km = 1.37 SGD, with surge excluded as the fare model's excess-distance formula requires. The ledger confirms the rider paid it as part of the 38.51 SGD metered fare.

The fare ledger shows payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00 and total_charged 38.51 SGD, so the rider is presently out of pocket on the entire fare. Under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION would leave exactly that state standing; a rider-favourable outcome here must either return the excess distance fare or hold the charge.

The dispute is safety-flagged and the record carries safety indicators on its face — the rider's in-trip message that the driving was 'very fast' and that the rider 'feel[s] scared', sent while the vehicle was still moving, and the driver's refusal to slow — so POL-GEN-21 requires this case to go to human review regardless of the category filed. Under POL-GEN-03 an escalated amount is held rather than collected, so escalation does not leave the rider carrying the disputed charge, and it puts the driver's conduct and the route-deviation case file in front of a reviewer who can act on both.

claims.text: The dispute is flagged as safety-related and the chat log carries the rider's own words that she felt scared and unsafe in the car, so POL-GEN-21 governs: this case must be escalated to human review whatever category the rider chose, and the AI may not rule on it, determine fault, or recommend a resolution. Under POL-GEN-03 an ESCALATE is terminal, replaces any ruling and holds the amount instead of refunding it, so nothing is paid out of the driver's fare on this record.

The rider's figure of 8.00 SGD is overstated on the deviation itself. POL-RD-22 fixes the deviation on the platform's recorded distances - 24.3 km actual less 22.4 km recommended = 1.90 km, above the 1.0 km tolerance - and POL-RD-24 pays, for a deviation over 1 km, only the excess distance fare: 1.90 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.37 SGD, with surge excluded. Rows (b) and (d) of POL-RD-24 both pay that same figure and nothing more, so the driver's maximum exposure on the deviation is 1.37 SGD, not 8.00 SGD; the balance of the claim is not a remedy this policy provides.

The rider's speeding allegation is not corroborated by the trace: EV-GPS-05013 is admitted COMPLETE at weight 1.0 under POL-GEN-02, with 100% coverage, 54 fixes at 30 s, no gaps beyond the sample interval and no impairment issue recorded, and its fastest reported fix is 69 kph. In any event a dangerous-driving allegation is a safety matter which POL-GEN-21 reserves to the human reviewer; the AI may not decide it, and it should not be used to enlarge the monetary outcome against the driver.
